name: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller
notes: The 97-byte report descriptor and the report 0x09 layout are reconstructed from two independent implementations that agree on every field, so no hardware capture was needed: VIIPER's device/ns2pro (descriptor.go item list, inputstate.go buildProReport / proButtonMap / packStick12) and SDL3's SDL_hidapi_switch2.c, the driver SDL routes 057E:2069 to. Three reports are declared. 0x05 is the 63-byte vendor blob a Nintendo protocol host reads, 0x09 is the structured gamepad view, 0x02 is output. Real hardware powers up emitting 0x09 (VIIPER device.go sets activeReportID = ReportIDPro at construction) and switches to 0x05 only when a host sends the subUSBSelectReport subcommand, so 0x09 is what this profile emits and it needs no handshake to be usable. LIMITATION, stated precisely because it is structural rather than a missing feature: SDL routes 057E:2069 to its dedicated SDL_hidapi_switch2 driver, whose USB init needs libusb plus the controller's second interface bound to WinUSB through MS OS 2.0 descriptors. A UMDF2 HID profile presents one HID interface and cannot offer that, so HIDAPI_DriverSwitch2_InitUSB fails, InitDevice returns false, and SDL_hidapijoystick.c cleans the driver up and closes the device. Reaching SDL's Switch 2 driver at all would require the composite USB backend, which this profile deliberately does not use. Whether SDL then surfaces the pad through its Windows joystick backend instead is NOT verified here. DirectInput, joy.cpl, WGI and anything parsing the HID report descriptor see a complete 21-button 4-axis gamepad without it. GR, GL and C are the Switch 2 additions absent from the original Switch Pro. Headset exists in report 0x05 only and has no bit in 0x09, which is why the descriptor declares 21 buttons plus 3 padding bits rather than 22 plus 2. Sticks are 12-bit, two axes packed into three shared bytes (packStick12), centre 0x0800. EVIDENCE ASYMMETRY, worth knowing before trusting this blindly: the report 0x05 button map is corroborated by three independent implementations (VIIPER commonButtonMap, SDL HandleSwitchProState, and switch2-controllers-linux ngc/protocol.py SWITCH_BUTTONS), which also explains the 0x10/0x20 gaps in its bytes 0 and 2 as the Joy-Con SR/SL rail buttons a Pro does not have. The report 0x09 map this profile actually emits has ONE source, VIIPER proButtonMap, because the other two consumers parse 0x05. 0x09 is still the right report to emit: 0x05 is an opaque vendor blob in the descriptor and would leave DirectInput and joy.cpl with nothing to read, whereas 0x09 is the structured view that makes the pad usable without any handshake.
